subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- November 24, 2026
body:
AcreetionOS CI now publishes ISOs automatically to the public mirror over SSH

The big news this week: Darren wired the GitLab pipeline to push fresh ISOs straight to the production ISO server via SSH, no manual steps required. The `publish:iso` job now runs with `GIT_STRATEGY: none` so it skips the redundant checkout and ships the artifact in under two minutes — meaning every merged MR can land a testable image on https://acreetionos.org/flash.html without anyone hitting a deploy button.

Development
Darren also cleaned up a batch of UI regressions in both the main acreetionos and acreetionos-xlibre repos: bottom-bar icons are clickable again, the welcome screen regained its missing pieces, and a pesky screen-detection bug in the fences utility got squashed. Natalie dropped the first commit of acreetionos-wallpapers, so expect a curated set of emerald-black and neon-purple backgrounds to land in the next ISO spin.

Community
Upstream Arch delivered seven stable kernel point-releases (7.3.6, 6.18.65 among them) and 7.4-rc4 hit the prepatch tree — our kernel config will pull those in during the next rebuild. CachyOS dropped their November release with fresh scheduler tunes; we’re watching their `cachyos-kernel` patches for any Cinnamon-relevant wins. Security-wise, the usual Monday batch from AlmaLinux and Arch proper (curl, expat, flatpak, etc.) is already mirrored in our repo.

Tip of the day
If you’re testing a nightly ISO from the new auto-publish flow, verify the SHA256 on the download page before writing to USB — the checksum file sits right next to the `.iso` link. And when you boot, hit `F2` at the Calamares screen to drop into a debug shell; `journalctl -f` there lets you watch the installer modules load in real time, handy for spotting the occasional XLibre probe race.
